headline.purpose: Landing section headings and the intake heading; final CTA up to 56px.

title.purpose: Open file name, dropzone prompt, landing step captions.

body.purpose: Everything Veil says: messages, status lines, chat questions, card titles.

button.purpose: Button labels, sentence case; 13px sm, 20px lg, 26px xl.

label.purpose: Silkscreen uppercase labels for fields and panels, chips, tabs, top bar links, step numbers.

tag.purpose: Placeholder text inside a black redaction bar.

numeral.purpose: Live counts and statistics in tabular figures; 20px counter, 12px totals, 10px line numbers.

document.purpose: Document lines on the paper sheet; all-caps headings at 600 13px tracked 0.06em.

field.purpose: Text the person types or pastes; placeholders stay in Pixelify.

shadows.name: pixel-drop
shadows.purpose: Raised button at rest. Hover: 0 6px 0 with translateY(-2px). Press: 0 0 0 with translateY(4px). Dark buttons cast quiet; buttons on ink panels cast #45443f.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: Pressable card on hover or focus (sample cards).

shadows.name: current-line-rule
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: 2px red rules around the line being redacted.

motion.name: ease-out-soft
motion.purpose: Default for movement: button rise and press (0.14s, press 0.05s), bar wipe (0.38s), popover in (0.18s), card lift (0.2s), gutter mark (0.25s).

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Arrivals: review bar rise (0.5s), Ask panel reveal (0.5s), landing captions (0.45s), statistic count-up (1.1s), victory pixel assembly (0.95s).

motion.name: colour-tween
motion.purpose: Background and text colour changes on hover and state.

motion.name: scroll-spring
motion.purpose: Landing pinned story; reversible on scroll up. Parallax layers are scroll-linked transforms.

motion.name: pass-tick
motion.value: 6000ms / line count, clamped 70ms to 380ms; 250ms hold before the review bar
motion.purpose: Advance of the line-by-line redaction pass.

motion.name: sprite-frame
motion.value: 0.6s steps(1, jump-none) infinite, two frames cross-swapped
motion.purpose: The only stepped timing: torches, pennants, wings. Also the spinner blink (0.9s steps(1)) and the two-frame guard idle (0.9s steps(2)).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: CSS: animation and transition durations 0.01ms, one iteration, no delay. JS: the pass resolves instantly; Motion useReducedMotion shows finished scenes, static parallax and final counts
motion.purpose: Every animation has a reduced-motion state.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Wider page padding; landing top bar links appear.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Landing grids go to columns; step titles and clouds appear.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: App columns: 240px rail / document / 340px Ask panel.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: App columns: 270px rail / document / 400px Ask panel.

pixelFrames.technique: border-image of a 3x3 SVG with empty corners, slice 1, stretched over a transparent 4px border (2px thin), background-clip padding-box
pixelFrames.dropzone: 8px ink dashes on a 4px line drawn with background gradients; red while a file is over it

sprites.rendering: one SVG path of horizontal runs per colour, shape-rendering crispEdges, whole-number scale

scales.icon: 2x (3x in lg and xl buttons, 5x in the dropzone)
scales.landing: 4x to 6x; castle fitted 3px to 7px per pixel

borders.focus: 3px solid var(--color-signal); offset 6px on buttons, 3px elsewhere

narrative.overview:
Veil is one pixel product on bone paper. Everything Veil says, every control, label and message, is drawn in bitmap: pixel type, 4px frames with notched corners, raised buttons that stand on a 4px pixel shadow and sink flat when pressed, icons on a 12-pixel grid. Everything that belongs to the person, their document, the text they paste and the answer an AI gives them, is set in a calm book serif on a paper sheet. The two materials never trade places, so a glance tells you whose words you are reading.

The palette is ink on warm off-white with one signal red. Red means the act of hiding a value or the commit that ends a task (New document, Approve all, Hide, Protect a document). Depth comes from inversion to ink, from pixel frames, and from the hard pixel shadow under things you can press; nothing is blurred and nothing is rounded.

Motion is eased, not stepped. Things that move travel on a soft ease-out or, on the landing story, on a scroll-linked spring that runs backwards when the visitor scrolls up. Stepped timing is kept for sprite frame swaps: torches, pennants, wings, the blinking spinner cells. The signature moment is the line-by-line redaction pass, where each personal value flashes red and a black bar wipes across it and drops a red placeholder tag; the second is the full-screen knight victory after Approve all.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials: pixel for Veil's voice, paper and serif for the person's content.
Bone and paper grounds, ink frames, one signal red for redaction and commit.
Notched 4px pixel frames on every container and control; 0px radius everywhere.
Raised pixel buttons with a hard 4px shadow that collapses on press.
Eased and spring movement; stepped timing only for sprite frames; a reduced-motion state for every animation.
Icons, pictograms and characters are character-grid sprites with crisp edges.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Signal red means redaction or commitment. It never decorates and never marks a category, and there is no second accent hue.

rules.name: The Red-On-Ink Rule
rules.body: On ink, red text is Soft Signal; on bone or paper, red text is Deep Signal. Full Signal is for fills, frames and marks.

rules.name: The Pixel and Paper Rule
rules.body: Everything Veil says is pixel: Pixelify Sans for headings, interface text, buttons and messages, Silkscreen for labels and numbers. Everything that is the user's document, pasted text or the AI's answer is paper: Source Serif 4. Never set a control in the serif, and never set the person's content in a pixel face.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Every live count (change counter, review totals, line numbers, statistics, training examples) is Silkscreen with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: A hard pixel shadow means "you can press this". It belongs only to buttons and pressable cards, it has zero blur, and it collapses when pressed.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: To raise a surface, frame it or invert it to ink. Never lift it with a soft shadow or a blur.

rules.name: The Whole Pixel Rule
rules.body: Sprites scale only by whole numbers and render with crisp edges. No anti-aliased or fractionally scaled sprite at rest.

rules.name: The Notched Frame Rule
rules.body: Containers and controls take the notched pixel frame, not a CSS border with square corners. Plain rules are for dividing columns and sections only.

dos: Do set everything Veil says in Pixelify Sans or Silkscreen, and everything that is the user's document, pasted text or the AI's answer in Source Serif 4.
Do frame containers and controls with the notched pixel frame (4px, 2px for chips, tabs and thin panels) and keep every corner at 0px.
Do give every button the 4px pixel drop that rises on hover and collapses on press; reserve the hard shadow for things you can press.

Do move things with eased or spring motion (soft ease-out cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.8, 0.2, 1) for state changes, expo ease-out for arrivals, springs for scroll-linked scenes), animating only transform, opacity and clip-path.
Do use stepped timing only for sprite frame swaps (torches, pennants, wings, spinner cells, a two-frame idle).
Do give every animation a reduced-motion state: the pass resolves instantly, CSS animations collapse to their end state, and scroll scenes show their finished frame.
Do keep signal red for redaction marks and commit actions, with Deep Signal for red text on light grounds and Soft Signal for red on ink.
Do draw icons, pictograms and characters as character-grid sprites at whole-number scales, in currentColor inside controls.
Do use Silkscreen with tabular figures for every live count.
donts: Don't add blurred or soft shadows, glows, backdrop blurs or rounded corners to any surface.
Don't put a hard pixel shadow or a hover lift on anything that cannot be pressed.
Don't animate movement with `steps()`; stepped movement reads as lag outside sprite frames.
Don't set controls, labels or messages in the serif, or the person's content in a pixel face.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or use red decoratively.
Don't set small text in full Signal on bone or paper; it does not reach 4.5:1.
Don't use stone or haze for text; they are fill, frame and sprite colours.
Don't use icon fonts or vector line icons; icons are pixel sprites.
Don't put a Silkscreen label above a headline as a kicker; labels name a field, a panel or a stage element.
